title: Discussion on tensile test procedures of high-strength bolts
abstract: The present study aims to investigate different bolt types, including intrinsically bolt breaking and thread-stripping failure modes, and their behavior under distinct possible test methods, such as the bolt with a 1-Nut assembly, the bolt with a 2-Nut assembly (equivalent to ISO 898-1), and the dogbone-shaped coupon specimen. To achieve this aim, 78 specimens — from distinct companies with different bolt types — were tested under direct tension, and finite element analyses were carried out to assess the local response. The findings highlighted the possibility of overestimating ultimate strength and predicting incorrect failure modes when utilizing the ISO 898-1 test method for HV bolts. In contrast, for bolts exhibiting bolt breaking, the ISO 898-1 test method is accurate. The ultimate strengths of bolts obtained using different test methods were compared, and the fallacies of some testing procedures were highlighted. The finite element studies yielded results consistent with the experimental data. Finally, some recommendations for testing bolts are suggested for practical usage.
